etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Latin cōnstrūctus, from cōnstruō (“to heap together”), from com- (“together”) + struō (“I heap up, pile”). Doublet of construe.

definitions.definition: (genetics) A segment of nucleic acid, created artificially, for transplantation into a target cell or tissue.
(transitive) To build or form (something) by assembling parts.
(transitive, grammar) To build (a sentence, an argument, etc.) by arranging words or ideas.

quote.text: The Vietnam War films are forms of memory that function to provide collective rememberings, to construct history, and to subsume within them the experience of the veterans.

definitions.definition: (transitive, geometry) To draw (a geometric figure) by following precise specifications and using geometric tools and techniques.
